questions.stem: When joining narrow boards edge to edge to make a wide table top, the joint used is a
options: widening joint such as a tongued and grooved or dowelled joint
questions.explanation: Widening (edge) joints such as butt, dowelled, tongued and grooved or rebated joints increase width; the others are framing or carcase joints.

questions.stem: Loose clothing and ties must not be worn near woodworking machines because they
options: can be caught by rotating parts and pull the operator in
questions.explanation: Rotating cutters and spindles can entangle loose items; overalls should be close-fitting.

questions.stem: The saw used for cutting tenons and other fine joints, with a stiffening strip along its back, is the
questions.explanation: Back saws (tenon and dovetail saws) have a steel or brass back for accurate joint cutting.

questions.stem: A plane iron is normally ground at about 25 degrees and then honed at about
questions.explanation: Honing at a slightly steeper angle (about 30 degrees) gives a strong cutting edge on the ground bevel.

questions.stem: The plane used for shaping curved edges such as chair legs and spoon handles is the
questions.explanation: The spokeshave has a short sole for convex and concave curves; the plough plane cuts grooves.

questions.stem: A boring bit that produces clean, flat-bottomed holes, such as for concealed hinges, is the
questions.explanation: Forstner bits are guided by their rim and leave a flat bottom; countersink bits recess screw heads.

questions.stem: The portable power tool used to cut mouldings, rebates and grooves on the edges of boards is the
questions.explanation: Routers use shaped cutters at high speed to make profiles and grooves.

questions.stem: The machine used to reduce prepared stock to an even thickness with its two faces parallel is the
questions.explanation: The surface planer flattens one face and edge; the thicknesser then makes the opposite face parallel at the set thickness.

questions.stem: The riving knife fitted behind a circular saw blade
options: keeps the kerf open to prevent the timber binding on the blade and kicking back
measures the width of the cut
holds the timber down on the table
sharpens the teeth as they pass
questions.explanation: If the kerf closes, the timber can grip the rising teeth and be thrown back at the operator.

questions.stem: Oiling and sharpening plane irons and saws at regular intervals, before they become blunt or rusty, is
questions.explanation: Preventive maintenance is scheduled care done to avoid failure.

questions.topic: West African Timbers in Common Use
questions.stem: Iroko (odum) is valued for outdoor work and furniture mainly because it is
options: durable and resistant to termites and decay
questions.explanation: Iroko is a durable hardwood; it is used for doors, window frames, furniture and boats.

questions.topic: West African Timbers in Common Use
questions.stem: A light, pale, easily worked hardwood often used for drawer sides, mouldings and light frames in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: Obeche is light and soft although botanically a hardwood; ebony is dense and black.

questions.topic: West African Timbers in Common Use
questions.stem: Botanically, timbers are classified as hardwoods or softwoods according to
options: the type of tree: broad-leaved trees give hardwoods and conifers give softwoods
questions.explanation: The classification is botanical; some hardwoods, such as obeche, are softer than some softwoods.

questions.stem: The method of conversion that gives the most stable boards with attractive figure but produces the most waste is
questions.explanation: Quarter-sawn boards shrink evenly and show ray figure but conversion is slower and wasteful.

questions.stem: Through-and-through sawing of a log is the
options: method that produces only quarter-sawn boards
cheapest and quickest method, with little waste
questions.explanation: Parallel cuts through the whole log are simple and economical, but many boards are flat-sawn and liable to cup.

questions.stem: A timber sample weighs 168 g before and 140 g after oven drying. Its moisture content is
questions.explanation: MC = (wet mass - dry mass) / dry mass x 100 = 28 / 140 x 100 = 20%; it is based on the oven-dry mass, not the wet mass.

questions.stem: A curvature of a board along its length on the face is called
questions.explanation: Bowing is lengthwise curve on the face; cupping is curvature across the width.

questions.stem: Radial cracks running from the pith of a log towards the bark are
questions.explanation: Star shakes radiate from the centre; ring shakes follow the growth rings.

questions.stem: The most effective method of applying preservative to timber for long-term outdoor use, such as electricity poles, is
options: pressure impregnation in a closed cylinder
questions.explanation: Pressure treatment forces preservative deep into the wood; surface methods give only shallow protection.

questions.stem: Plywood is made by gluing an odd number of thin veneers together with
options: all the grain running the same way
the grain of adjacent layers at right angles
questions.explanation: Cross-banding the grain makes plywood strong in both directions and stable; the odd number balances it.

questions.stem: In preparing timber by hand, the FIRST surface to be planed true and marked as the face side is
questions.explanation: The face side is planed first, then the face edge square to it; these are the reference surfaces for marking out.

questions.stem: Using the rule that a tenon should be about one-third of the thickness of the rail, the tenon for a 45 mm thick rail should be about
questions.explanation: One-third of 45 mm = 15 mm, leaving enough wood in the mortised member on each side.

questions.stem: The joint commonly used to fix the rails of a table or chair to its legs is the
questions.explanation: Mortise and tenon joints give strong framing; dovetails are used in boxes and drawers.

questions.stem: The joint used to fix a drawer front to the drawer sides so that the joint is NOT seen from the front is the
questions.explanation: In the lapped dovetail the tails stop short of the front face, hiding the joint.

questions.stem: French polish is made by dissolving
questions.explanation: French polish is shellac in spirit applied with a rubber; it gives a high gloss but is easily damaged by heat and water.

questions.stem: For the final smoothing of a table top before finishing, a woodworker should use abrasive paper of
options: any grade, as grade does not matter
questions.explanation: Coarse grades remove material fast; fine grades give the smooth final surface.

questions.stem: The two-part adhesive made of a resin and a hardener that bonds wood to metal, glass and ceramics is
questions.explanation: Epoxies cure chemically and bond dissimilar materials; PVA is a general-purpose wood glue.

questions.stem: Contact (rubber-based) adhesive is used to fix plastic laminate to a worktop by
options: coating one surface and cramping for 24 hours while wet
coating both surfaces, allowing them to become touch-dry, then pressing them together
soaking the laminate in the adhesive overnight
questions.explanation: Contact adhesive bonds instantly on contact once the solvent has evaporated, so positioning must be accurate.

questions.stem: The hinge that runs along the full length of a lid or fall-flap is the
questions.explanation: Piano hinges support the whole edge; tee hinges are used on gates and ledged doors.

questions.stem: Which non-wood material is used to make glazed cabinet doors?
questions.explanation: Glass gives transparency for display cabinets; leather is used for upholstery coverings.

questions.stem: In hammer veneering, the veneer is laid with
options: epoxy and a caul press only
hot animal glue, pressed down with a veneer hammer
questions.explanation: Hot animal glue lets the veneer be pressed and squeezed flat with the veneer hammer before it gels.

questions.stem: Gluing thin strips of wood together over a curved former to produce a curved component is
questions.explanation: Laminated bending holds its shape when the glue sets; solid bending softens the wood with steam.

questions.stem: In first angle orthographic projection, the plan is drawn
options: to the left of the end elevation only
in the same position as the front elevation
questions.explanation: First angle places the plan below the front view; third angle places it above.

questions.stem: The first step in solving a design problem for a customer is to
options: identify and analyse the need or problem
questions.explanation: Design begins with a clear statement and analysis of the problem before ideas, construction and evaluation.

questions.stem: The tool used to pull jute webbing tight across a chair frame before tacking is the
questions.explanation: The webbing stretcher tensions the webbing which supports the padding.

questions.stem: Turning a bowl on the lathe with the blank screwed to a metal plate on the headstock spindle is
questions.explanation: Bowls and platters are turned on a faceplate; table legs are turned between centres.

questions.stem: A carving in which the design projects from a flat background is a
questions.explanation: In relief carving the background is cut away; incised carving cuts the design into the surface.

questions.stem: Making a decorative picture or pattern from pieces of different-coloured veneers fitted together like a jigsaw is
questions.explanation: Marquetry assembles veneer pieces into a sheet design; inlaying sets material into recesses cut in solid wood.

questions.stem: A device that holds the workpiece in position AND guides the cutting tool during repeated production is a
questions.explanation: A jig guides the tool as well as locating the work; a fixture only holds the work.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a business opportunity in woodworking?
questions.explanation: Furniture making, upholstery, wood turning, carving and timber merchandising are woodwork businesses.

questions.stem:
(a) Define timber seasoning and state two reasons for seasoning timber. [3 marks]
(b) A timber sample weighed 85 g before drying and 68 g after drying to constant mass in an oven. Calculate its moisture content. [3 marks]
(c) State two advantages and two disadvantages of air (natural) seasoning. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) The controlled removal of moisture from freshly cut timber to a suitable moisture content for its use
2 marks: (a) Any two, 1 mark each: reduces shrinkage and movement in use; increases strength; reduces weight; makes timber resistant to fungi and insects; improves gluing and finishing; makes working easier
3 marks: (b) MC = (wet - dry)/dry x 100 (1) = (85 - 68)/68 x 100 (1) = 25% (1)
2 marks: (c) Advantages, any two: cheap; needs little skill/equipment; large quantities can be dried; fewer seasoning defects if well stacked
2 marks: (c) Disadvantages, any two: slow; moisture content limited by weather/humidity; needs large space; timber exposed to attack and degrade while drying
questions.explanation: Seasoning removes moisture to suit the timber's use, reducing movement, weight and decay. MC = 17/68 x 100 = 25%. Air seasoning is cheap and simple but slow, weather-dependent and space-consuming.

questions.stem:
(a) Name two widening joints and two angle (framing) joints. [4 marks]
(b) Describe the procedure for marking out and cutting a through mortise and tenon joint. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Widening, any two, 1 mark each: butt; dowelled; tongued and grooved; loose tongue; rebated butt
2 marks: (a) Angle/framing, any two, 1 mark each: mortise and tenon; bridle; halving; dowelled butt; dovetail; housing
6 marks: (b) 1 mark each: prepare stock with face side and face edge marked; mark tenon length and mortise length with try square and knife; set mortise gauge to chisel width (about 1/3 of thickness) and gauge both pieces from face side; chop the mortise with mortise chisel and mallet, working from both sides; saw the tenon cheeks with tenon saw on the waste side, then cut the shoulders; test fit, glue and cramp, checking for square
questions.explanation: Widening: butt, dowelled, tongue and groove. Framing: mortise and tenon, bridle, halving. Prepare stock, mark lengths, set the mortise gauge to one-third thickness and gauge from the face side, chop the mortise from both sides, saw cheeks then shoulders, fit, glue and cramp square.

questions.stem:
(a) State four safety precautions when using a circular sawing machine. [4 marks]
(b) Distinguish between the surface planer and the thicknesser. [4 marks]
(c) State two items of routine maintenance for woodworking machines. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) Any four, 1 mark each: crown guard and riving knife correctly fitted; use push stick for narrow/short pieces; blade sharp and set correctly; stand to one side of the blade line; do not reach over the blade; switch off and isolate before adjusting; wear goggles/ear protection and close-fitting clothing; only trained persons
2 marks: (b) Surface planer: produces a flat face and an edge square to it (truing); timber is fed by hand over the cutter block on the table
2 marks: (b) Thicknesser: makes the second face parallel to the first and reduces timber to a set thickness; timber is fed automatically by rollers under the cutter block
2 marks: (c) Any two, 1 mark each: clean dust and resin; lubricate moving parts; sharpen/replace blades and cutters; check belts and guards; check electrical cables and switches
questions.explanation: Circular saw safety: guards and riving knife, push stick, sharp blade, stand aside, isolate before adjusting, PPE. The surface planer trues a face and edge; the thicknesser brings the opposite face parallel to a set thickness with power feed. Maintenance: clean, lubricate, sharpen, check belts and wiring.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain what is meant by a timber defect. [2 marks]
(b) For each of the following defects, state one cause and one way of preventing it: (i) cupping (ii) knots (iii) end splits (iv) dry rot. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Any irregularity or abnormality in timber that reduces its strength, durability, appearance or usefulness
2 marks: (b)(i) Cupping: unequal shrinkage across the width (tangential shrinkage greater than radial), especially in flat-sawn boards; prevent by proper stacking/weighting, quarter-sawing, controlled seasoning
2 marks: (b)(ii) Knots: bases of branches enclosed in the trunk as the tree grows; reduce by pruning young trees/selecting clear timber; cut out in conversion
2 marks: (b)(iii) End splits: rapid drying from the end grain during seasoning; prevent by sealing ends with paint/wax and slow, controlled drying
2 marks: (b)(iv) Dry rot: fungal attack on damp timber in poorly ventilated conditions; prevent by keeping moisture content low, good ventilation and preservative treatment
questions.explanation: A defect is any abnormality that lowers the strength, durability or appearance of timber. Cupping from unequal shrinkage - stack and season carefully. Knots from branches - prune or select clear timber. End splits from fast end drying - seal ends. Dry rot from fungi in damp, unventilated conditions - keep dry, ventilate, preserve.

questions.stem:
A stool has: 4 legs, each 750 mm x 50 mm x 50 mm; 4 rails, each 500 mm x 75 mm x 25 mm; 1 top, 600 mm x 600 mm x 20 mm (finished sizes).
(a) Prepare a cutting list showing the item, number, length, width and thickness. [3 marks]
(b) Calculate the total volume of timber in cubic metres. [4 marks]
(c) If the timber costs ₦400,000 per cubic metre, calculate the cost of the timber. [2 marks]
(d) Why are allowances added to finished sizes when ordering timber? [1 mark]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) Cutting list correctly tabulated: legs 4 off 750 x 50 x 50; rails 4 off 500 x 75 x 25; top 1 off 600 x 600 x 20 (1 mark per item)
1 mark: (b) Legs: 4 x 0.75 x 0.05 x 0.05 = 0.0075 m^3
1 mark: (b) Rails: 4 x 0.5 x 0.075 x 0.025 = 0.00375 m^3
1 mark: (b) Top: 0.6 x 0.6 x 0.02 = 0.0072 m^3
1 mark: (b) Total = 0.0075 + 0.00375 + 0.0072 = 0.01845 m^3
2 marks: (c) Cost = 0.01845 x 400,000 = ₦7,380
1 mark: (d) To allow for planing, saw cuts, squaring ends and defects so that the finished size can still be obtained
questions.explanation: Volume: legs 0.0075 + rails 0.00375 + top 0.0072 = 0.01845 m^3; cost = ₦7,380. Allowances cover planing, kerf, end trimming and defects.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the construction of (i) plywood (ii) blockboard. [4 marks]
(b) State three advantages of manufactured boards over solid timber. [3 marks]
(c) State one use each of plywood, blockboard and chipboard. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) Plywood: an odd number of thin veneers glued together with the grain of adjacent layers at right angles
2 marks: (a)(ii) Blockboard: core of solid wood strips (about 25 mm wide) glued edge to edge, faced on both sides with one or two layers of veneer at right angles
3 marks: (b) Any three, 1 mark each: available in large sizes; dimensionally stable/no shrinkage or warping; uniform strength in both directions; makes use of low-grade timber/waste; free from natural defects; economical
3 marks: (c) 1 mark each: plywood - panels, ceilings, drawer bottoms, boat building; blockboard - doors, shelves, table tops, partitions; chipboard - kitchen cabinets, wardrobe carcasses, flooring
questions.explanation: Plywood: odd number of cross-grained veneers. Blockboard: solid strip core faced with veneers. Boards come in large, stable, defect-free sheets of uniform strength. Uses: plywood for panels and ceilings; blockboard for doors and shelves; chipboard for cabinets and flooring.
